eyebrow: Destinations / Africa & the Indian Ocean / Morocco
title: City, mountain, desert
standfirst: Three landscapes within a few hours of each other, which few countries can offer.

blocks.heading: A riad taken whole
paras: The medina is exhausting as a visitor and delightful as a resident, and the difference is having a house inside it.
A riad with its own staff turns the city from something to get through into the reason for the trip.

blocks.heading: The Atlas, not just the desert
blocks.caption: Mountain lodges two hours from the city.
paras: Everyone books the desert and almost nobody books the mountains, which are closer, cooler and in some ways better.
Three nights in the Atlas breaks the heat and gives the walking that the desert cannot.

blocks.heading: One night under canvas
blocks.caption: The desert camps are best at one night, not three.
paras: The dunes are extraordinary for an evening and a sunrise. By the second afternoon most people have had enough sand.
We build one night in, not three, and we put the good bedding and the good cook in it.

blocks.heading: Questions members ask
blocks.intro: The ones that come up nearly every time.

a: March to May and September to November. The desert is best in winter; the coast is best in summer.
Yes, and overwhelming. A guide for the first morning makes the rest of the week navigable.
Eight to ten nights for city, mountain and desert without rushing any of them.

blocks.heading: We are ready when you are
paras: Every itinerary starts with a conversation about what you actually want from the days, and works backwards to houses, guides and timing from there.
